## Origins and attribution

Michael Hallquist developed these notes for Penn State's graduate structural equation modeling course.

Benjamin Johnson contributed to the full SEM lectures and examples. Nate Hall adapted the Onyx tutorial with permission from Benjamin N. Johnson. Michael Clark's teaching material informed the latent-variable score simulation and growth-modeling chapters. The MIMIC tutorial adapts Angelos Markos's supplemental Brown Chapter 7 code (2012). Other contributions and source links remain credited in their respective chapters, including Aidan Wright's covariance example and Nick Michalak's mediation demonstration.

## Build and preview

Install Quarto and R, then install the required R packages from the repository root:

```bash
Rscript scripts/install_packages.R
quarto render
quarto preview
```

The rendered collection is written to `_site/`. Source documents execute relative to their own directories, so examples use portable relative paths. Package installation is an explicit setup step and never runs automatically inside a lecture.

## Mplus examples

The multilevel chapter reads saved teaching outputs by default. It can therefore render without Mplus. The `.inp`, `.dat`, and `.out` files are available beside that chapter for inspection and comparison. A license and executable are needed only to re-estimate those models:

```bash
SEM_RUN_MPLUS=true MPLUS_COMMAND=/path/to/mplus quarto render 15_multilevel/multilevel_sem.qmd
```

The chapter also contains a runnable lavaan example. Consult the [lavaan multilevel documentation](https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/multilevel.html) for capabilities supported by your installed version.

## Simulation depth

The factor-score tutorial uses a small number of replications for a routine render. Increase the number when investigating Monte Carlo behavior:

```bash
SEM_SIM_REPS=1000 quarto render 05_psychometrics/lv_sim.qmd
```

The default simulation illustrates the method; it does not provide precise simulation-study estimates.
